findings.where: Article specimen: the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', against the type pair's note 'Headings in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide like a drawing title' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The tile's own rule says headings are ExtraBold tracked capitals, and the hero name and the OVERPASS sample follow it. The one real heading in the article specimen is set in bold mixed case with no tracking. So the tile shows two heading styles and does not say which one an article title should use.
findings.who_objects: The designers of the layout round (#8 round 2) and Angélique, who have to draw and edit articles within this look. The tile is the type spec, and here it contradicts itself on the most common heading on the site.

findings.where: Article specimen: the date line 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024' compared with the PDF row 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF' just below it
findings.fault: The two dates in the same specimen use different faces. The article date is in proportional Overpass and the PDF date is in Overpass Mono. That breaks the stated rule that mono is for dates, and like text is not set alike. The separators also change between '•' and '·' within the one PDF line, and the hero and the motion title use them inconsistently too.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article page sees two date styles a few lines apart, so the meta line looks unfinished. A later designer cannot tell which date treatment is meant.

findings.where: Hero, the lines under 'MARK M. MOSELEY': 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's role is set in the same size, weight, case, tracking and colour as the drawing-sheet caption beneath it. The one line that says what he does has no more rank than the drawing jargon. On the phone the line breaks after 'A-A •', which leaves the separator dangling at the end of a line.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff scanning the first screen to see who this is. 'Infrastructure advisor' reads as one more drawing label next to 'Longitudinal section A-A', not as Mark's role.

findings.where: Small explanatory text: the palette swatch notes, the texture caption, the type-pair notes, the motion sketch's easing note and total note (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The notes are set in light weight at caption size, in pale blue, over a busy grid. The light strokes thin out and break up against the grid lines, so these lines read much more weakly than the Regular body text in the article.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reading the tile to understand the look, Mark included. The notes carry the reasoning, and they are the hardest lines on the page to read.
